one_liner: Rust log and metrics pipeline whose 2019 first-party tests beat Fluent Bit 1.1.0; the current-version regex run loses.
what_it_does: Vector is Datadog's observability data pipeline: a standalone daemon that collects, transforms and routes logs and metrics (traces are still in progress), deployed as a per-host agent or a central aggregator. Pipelines are a YAML, TOML or JSON DAG of sources, transforms (VRL 'remap' programs, dedupe, aggregate and others) and sinks, hot-reloadable with SIGHUP. It is not a library: it replaces Fluent Bit, Fluentd, Filebeat or Logstash at the deployment level, with its own configuration language and plugin set.
how_it_is_fast: Each DAG node is an async task on the multi-threaded Tokio runtime, connected by bounded channels with backpressure by default. Stateless transforms such as remap are inlined into the source task, and each source defines its own unit of concurrency (the socket source per open connection, the file source per tailed file), so throughput spreads over all vCPUs without tuning. In the harness the advantage is mostly that parallelism: on the 2-vCPU c5.large, Vector's system-wide CPU usr peaks at 93.5-96.5 while Fluent Bit 1.1.0 peaks at 49.8-53.2, about one core. The project's sizing guide also says VRL compiles to machine code; that claim was not checked here.
when_to_use: A multi-core agent or aggregator ingesting many TCP or syslog connections or many tailed files, where you want throughput to scale over every vCPU with no worker tuning (the sizing guide suggests at least 2 vCPUs for agents and 4 for aggregators).
Replacing Logstash or Fluentd (JVM or Ruby): in the same harness Vector moved 69.9 MiB/s TCP to TCP against Logstash's 10 and Fluentd's 3.9, at 171.6 MiB peak memory against 725.4 and 293.6 MiB.

Pipelines that need heavy routing, enrichment and many sinks in one binary, with disk buffers and end-to-end delivery guarantees (the README's correctness table shows Vector passing disk-buffer persistence, copytruncate rotation and SIGHUP tests that Fluent Bit 1.1.0 failed).
Memory-constrained hosts with spare cores: peak memory in the 2019 TCP rows was 171-233 MiB for Vector against 614.8 MiB to 1.1 GiB for Fluent Bit 1.1.0.
when_not_to_use: CPU-capped edge or sidecar agents limited to about one core: per core, Fluent Bit is ahead. In the only current-version harness row (regex parsing), Fluent Bit 3.2.7 moves 20.5 MiB/s at a 50.8 CPU usr peak and Vector 0.55.0 moves 13.2 MiB/s at 95, roughly 3x less throughput per unit of CPU (derived from page data).
Regex-heavy parsing at line rate, where Vector 0.55.0 is 1.55x slower than Fluent Bit 3.2.7 on the same Apache-log regex.

When CPU per event matters: VictoriaMetrics' public log-collectors-benchmark run of 2026-09-17 (Kubernetes, about 10.8k logs/s) measured Vector 0.58.0 at 0.288 cores and 111 MB average memory, against 0.204 cores and 56 MB for Fluent Bit 5.0.9 (about 1.4x more CPU, derived).
Embedding log shipping inside a C or C++ program: Vector is a separate daemon with no C API.

Many mostly idle TCP or TLS connections: open issues #26492 (idle connections starve busy ones because the RequestLimiter is capped at num_threads()) and #23230 (TLS source degrades once connections exceed CPU cores); #23546 reports kubernetes_logs capped near 30k events/s against 120k for the file source.

integration.form: standalone daemon binary (.deb/.rpm packages and container images); not a linkable library
integration.dependencies: none at run time for the packaged binary as installed by the harness (vector_<version>-1_amd64.deb); building from source needs the Rust workspace's crate dependencies
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 (harness packages); the sizing guide also recommends ARM64 (Graviton, Cobalt); other platforms not checked here
integration.thread_safety: multi-threaded Tokio runtime that uses all vCPUs automatically; stateful task transforms (dedupe, aggregate) are not parallelized
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it covers the same roles as Fluent Bit (TCP, file and HTTP sources and sinks, parsing), but the configuration format, transform language and plugin set differ, so a migration means rewriting configs

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the 2.2x File to TCP row: the winning metric 'Disk Thrpt (avg)' is the dstat block-device read rate on the subject (disk_read_avg in bin/compare), not bytes delivered. Vector read 4.6 GiB from disk but sent only 2.3 GiB over the network, while Fluent Bit read 2 GiB and sent 2 GiB. On bytes sent the gap is about 1.15x (derived from page data), and the checked-in configs have Fluent Bit emitting json_lines while Vector emits raw text, so even the byte counts are not like-for-like.

Core-count asymmetry: CPU usr in the tables is system-wide on a 2-vCPU c5.large. Fluent Bit 1.1.0 peaks at 49.8-53.2 in every row (about one core) and Vector at 93.5-96.5 (both cores), so the TCP to Blackhole (1.34x) and TCP to HTTP (1.36x) wins come largely from using the second core.

The published rows cannot be rerun as published. The harness README says it is under construction and that some performance tests may be broken. Current configs are YAML for modern Vector, and Fluent Bit now comes from the jammy apt repository, whereas the 2019 rows ran vector 0.2.0 (TOML configs; only tcp_to_blackhole keeps a vector.old.toml) against fluentbit 1.1.0. The multi_file configuration now creates 20 files of 250 MiB where the case README says 10. Each subject is one 60 s run with no variance (TCP to HTTP shows 'Test count 1'), and no compiler, flags or CPU model are given.

The README tagline 'up to 10x faster than every alternative' is not supported against Fluent Bit by its own table: the best Fluent Bit row is 1.36x (or 2.2x on the disk-read metric above), there is a tie on TCP to TCP, and the current-version regex row is a loss.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling is a log or metrics router. Unlike the single-command replacements (fd, cpz, rmz, tac), whose wins are timed on one workload, Vector's figures are whole-product, mostly from 2019 and driven by parallelism, so pick it as a multi-core replacement for Logstash or Fluentd, or for its pipeline features, rather than for raw per-core speed over Fluent Bit.
verified_claims_summary: In the first-party vector-test-harness (AWS c5.large subject, 10 c5.large producers for TCP to Blackhole and 5 for Regex Parsing, 60 s, one run per subject, dstat metrics, no compiler, flags or CPU model), vector 0.2.0 in 2019 beat Fluent Bit 1.1.0 on TCP to Blackhole (86 vs 64.4 MiB/s received) and TCP to HTTP (26.7 vs 19.6) and tied on TCP to TCP (69.9 vs 67.1). Its 'File to TCP' 76.7 vs 35 MiB/s is a disk-read rate, and on bytes sent that row is 2.3 vs 2.0 GiB (about 1.15x). The only current-version row has Vector 0.55.0 1.55x slower than Fluent Bit 3.2.7 at regex parsing. A third-party run by VictoriaMetrics (2026-09-17, Vector 0.58.0 vs Fluent Bit 5.0.9 on Kubernetes) found Vector using about 1.4x the CPU at about 10.8k logs/s. At peak load Vector sustained 32,057 logs/s with no loss, while Fluent Bit reached 41,222 logs/s before it was OOM-killed with 1,133,131 logs lost.
status_note: Actively maintained by Datadog (14,423 commits, last commit 2026-10-09 per the verifier, master at 0.60.0-dev), MPL-2.0 and 22.7k stars, so it is production-ready as a daemon. Its README performance table, however, dates from 2019 apart from the regex row, and the harness behind it describes itself as under construction.
